blocks.raw: <WikiMistakeList mistakes={["Using A307 bolts in primary friction-grip connections: A307 is for bearing work (loose bolts). A325 or A490 are required for preload and friction. Confusing the two invalidates connection capacity.","Calculating edge distance from the edge of the bolt head rather than the bolt _center_: AISC J3.2 specifies distance from hole center to member edge. Bolts heads are larger; the critical clearance is to the hole.","Spacing bolts at exactly 3 d instead of minimum 2.67 d and calling it code-compliant: the rule is ≥ 2.67 d for tearout prevention. Always add safety margin.","Assuming all four bolt hole types have the same clamping behavior: standard and oversized holes have different clearances and load paths. Slotted holes reduce clamping area and should not be used in high-shear connections.","Neglecting to account for net section in tension: after deducting bolt holes, the remaining area must have sufficient strength. Large holes or closely spaced bolts can render the net section inadequate."]} />
